::: {#exm-auto-widths}

#### Wider networks on the Auto data

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
auto = pd.read_csv("data/auto.csv")
hp = torch.tensor(auto["horsepower"].to_numpy(), dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)
mpg = torch.tensor(auto["mpg"].to_numpy(), dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)
hp_scaled = (hp - hp.mean()) / hp.std()
print(auto[["horsepower", "mpg"]].head(3))


def fit_width(width, steps=3000):
    # Fit a one-hidden-layer ReLU network of `width` units to mpg on horsepower.
    torch.manual_seed(2)
    net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1, width), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(width, 1))
    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(net.parameters(), lr=0.01)
    for step in range(steps):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss = nn.functional.mse_loss(net(hp_scaled), mpg)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
    return net, loss.item()


grid = torch.linspace(hp.min().item(), hp.max().item(), 300).unsqueeze(1)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.scatter(hp, mpg, s=6, color="gray", alpha=0.6)
auto_mse = {}
for width in [1, 3, 20]:
    net, auto_mse[width] = fit_width(width)
    with torch.no_grad():
        ax.plot(grid, net((grid - hp.mean()) / hp.std()), label=f"width {width}")
ax.set_xlabel("horsepower")
ax.set_ylabel("mpg")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
print(auto_mse)
```

The [Auto data](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/course-overview.html#def-auto-data) hold `r nrow(py$auto)` cars from the UCI Auto MPG dataset [@quinlan1993auto],
from a local copy, [`data/auto.csv`](data/auto.csv), of the version in lds.
Each network fits miles per gallon on horsepower, rescaled to mean 0 and standard deviation 1,
by 3,000 steps of gradient descent on the mean squared error.
With 1 unit the fit can bend only once,
and its training mean squared error is `r sprintf("%.1f", py$auto_mse[["1"]])`.
With 3 units it is `r sprintf("%.1f", py$auto_mse[["3"]])`, and with 20 units `r sprintf("%.1f", py$auto_mse[["20"]])`,
as the extra bends follow the curve of the data a little more closely.
@thm-universal-approximation says that enough units can follow any continuous curve;
it does not say that following the [training data](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-data) more closely predicts new cars better.

:::
